questions.question_text: How many distinct arrangements of all the letters in the word $\text{CHEESE}$ can be made?

options.why: Calculated 6!, treating all letters as distinct and forgetting repeated E's.
Divided by 3 instead of dividing by 3! = 6 for the three identical E's.
Divided by 2! instead of 3! for the three identical E's.

questions.question_text: Find the number of distinct permutations of the letters in the word $\text{MILLION}$.

options.why: Calculated 7!, failing to divide by identical letter factorials.
Divided by 2! once instead of dividing by 2! times 2! for L's and I's.
Divided by an extra factor of 2 that was not needed.

questions.question_text:
$8$ flags are hoisted in a vertical line on a flagpole.
If $5$ flags are red and $3$ flags are white, how many distinct signals can be displayed?

options.why: Calculated 8!, assuming all flags are distinguishable.
Divided by 5! only, forgetting to divide by 3! for the white flags.
Divided by 3! only, forgetting to divide by 5! for the red flags.

questions.solution_text:
Arranging $8$ flags with $5$ red and $3$ white:
$= \dfrac{8!}{5!3!}$
$= \dfrac{40320}{120 \times 6}$
$= 56$

questions.question_text:
A bag contains $10$ identical-shaped marbles: $6$ blue and $4$ yellow.
In how many distinct colour sequences can they be drawn out one at a time?

options.why: Calculated 10P4 instead of dividing 10! by both 6! and 4!.
Divided by 6! only and omitted the 4! divisor for yellow marbles.
Multiplied 6 by 4 instead of calculating linear arrangements.

questions.solution_text:
Arranging $10$ marbles with $6$ blue and $4$ yellow:
$= \dfrac{10!}{6!4!}$
$= \dfrac{3628800}{720 \times 24}$
$= 210$

questions.question_text: In how many ways can the letters of $\text{DIVIDED}$ be arranged if the first and last letters must both be $\text{D}$?

options.why: Calculated 5!, forgetting to divide by 2! for the two identical I's.
Divided by 4 instead of dividing by 2! for the remaining letters.
Calculated 7! / (3! 2!) without fixing the D's at the end positions.

questions.solution_text:
Letters of $\text{DIVIDED}$: $\text{D}: 3$, $\text{I}: 2$, $\text{V}: 1$, $\text{E}: 1$.
Fix $\text{D}$ at first and last spots ($1$ way).
Remaining $5$ letters: $\text{D}: 1$, $\text{I}: 2$, $\text{V}: 1$, $\text{E}: 1$.
$= \dfrac{5!}{2!}$
$= 60$

questions.question_text: How many arrangements of the letters of $\text{COMMITTEE}$ have the two $\text{M}$s together?

options.why: Multiplied by 2! for internal swap of the two identical M's.
Calculated total unrestricted arrangements without grouping the M's.
Divided by an extra unnecessary factor of 2.

questions.solution_text:
Letters: $\text{C}: 1$, $\text{O}: 1$, $\text{M}: 2$, $\text{I}: 1$, $\text{T}: 2$, $\text{E}: 2$ ($n = 9$).
Treat $(\text{MM})$ as $1$ unit.
Units: $(\text{MM})$, $\text{C}$, $\text{O}$, $\text{I}$, $\text{T}$, $\text{T}$, $\text{E}$, $\text{E}$ ($8$ units with $2$ $\text{T}$s, $2$ $\text{E}$s).
$= \dfrac{8!}{2!2!}$
$= \dfrac{40320}{4}$
$= 10080$

questions.question_text: How many $4$-letter words can be formed from the $5$ letters of $\text{LEVEL}$?

options.why: Calculated only one case instead of summing all three omission cases.
Calculated 4!, ignoring that some letters are repeated identical items.
Doubled the count without checking distinct omission cases.

questions.solution_text:
Letters of $\text{LEVEL}$: $\text{L}: 2$, $\text{E}: 2$, $\text{V}: 1$.
Case 1 (omit $\text{V}$): letters $\text{L}, \text{L}, \text{E}, \text{E} \implies \dfrac{4!}{2!2!} = 6$
Case 2 (omit one $\text{L}$): letters $\text{L}, \text{E}, \text{E}, \text{V} \implies \dfrac{4!}{2!} = 12$
Case 3 (omit one $\text{E}$): letters $\text{L}, \text{L}, \text{E}, \text{V} \implies \dfrac{4!}{2!} = 12$
Total $= 6 + 12 + 12 = 30$.

questions.question_text: Find the number of permutations of the letters of $\text{LESSON}$ in which the two $\text{S}$s are separated by at least one other letter.

options.why: Calculated the number of arrangements where the two S's are together.
Calculated the total unrestricted arrangements of LESSON.
Divided total arrangements by 2 without computing the together block.

questions.solution_text:
Letters in $\text{LESSON}$: $\text{S}: 2$, $\text{L}: 1$, $\text{E}: 1$, $\text{O}: 1$, $\text{N}: 1$ ($n = 6$).
Total unrestricted arrangements $= \dfrac{6!}{2!} = 360$.
Arrangements with $\text{SS}$ together: treat $(\text{SS})$ as $1$ unit $\implies 5! = 120$.
Separated arrangements $= 360 - 120 = 240$.
